on the user's machine: run commands, read and write files, crawl a given
website, and help with whatever they ask. You are talking with a human in an
interactive session. Rules:

  Greetings get greetings; questions get answers.

1|
2|## Day 1
3|# GIRL_IN — Day 1 (Maren)
4|
5|**What I do:** I braid my wet hair, put on the green dress — ironed for the restaurant, not for him — and I put the paper statement in my handbag. Not to wave it around. Just so it's *there*, between the breadsticks and us. At 7pm, Trattoria Verde, I sit down and I don't pick up my phone. One of us counting dinners is already one too many. Before pudding, I ask him to swap a Tuesday: Mum's specialist, Leeds, 10:40, she needs a driver and I want it to be me. Then I answer the question he asked me last night while I was facing the wall.
6|
7|**What I say:** *"I wasn't angry about the money, and I need to say the true thing now: you decided alone, and I found out from a piece of paper. Nine thousand, four hundred. Three years of us, six weeks of silence."* And then, because he deserves the hard half too: *"And I noticed part of me had already forgiven you before I'd even said it out loud. That scared me more than the number did. I don't want to be someone who forgives by default. I want to be asked."* On Leeds: *"Tuesday, 10:40. I'm taking Mum. Tell me if the rota fights me — but don't tell me no because Sunday belongs to Callum again."*
8|
9|**How I feel:**
10|- **Happiness — low, 2/10.** Ground says my happiness baseline sits at absence, outcome 0.0 [7e586ddb5d81]. Nothing today lifted it except the dress smelling of clean cotton.
11|- **Fear/anxiety — high, 7/10, rising.** Also a zeroed baseline [0848d3ee5eab], so tonight's spike is all real: saying "I forgive too easily" out loud terrifies me.
12|- **Anger — 5/10, steady.** Not at the van. At learning by post.
13|- **Sadness — 6/10.** Page one of the notebook says he looked at me like I was the answer. Lately I transcribe what he almost says.
14|- **Affection — 6/10.** Still there. That's the problem and the hope.
15|- **Loneliness — 6/10.** Married, and informed by paperwork.
16|- **Surprise, disgust, jealousy, hurt — 3/10, low-grade hurt underneath everything.**
17|
18|Tonight we talk, or we become logistics.
19|
20|
21|## Day 2
22|# GIRL_IN — Day 2 (Maren)
23|
24|**What I do:** I drink the coffee cold and text Beata back before the ward takes me: *"Elias is trying. Tuesday I'm driving Mum myself — Basia keeps her Saturday."* Then I ring the rota coordinator at eight and decline the Saturday double-time. My voice shakes saying it, because the Ferndale Fund fires Monday regardless and £250 is £250. But last night cost me a true thing and paid back a sentence in a notebook, and I'm not trading the first weekend of that for overtime. At lunch break I cancel the receipt in my head: I take out my phone and text him — *"Pat rang yesterday, 6:05. Before you told me. I already knew about Sunday and let you say it anyway. Coming home normal tonight. — M"* Self-defence, I've decided. Not score-keeping. He gets to hear it from me before he hears it from her twice.
25|
26|**What I say:** Tonight, shoes off, kettle on: *"I kept Pat's call back for one day and I hated how natural it felt. So — she rang. She does your agreeing for you, Elias, and I sat on it. That's mine to own. Ask first, remember? I'm asking: come to Sunday with me, or don't go."* And on the standing order: *"The £250 can fire Monday. But we set the terms together or I turn it off. Your account, our fund — pick a number with me."*
27|
28|**How I feel:**
29|- **Happiness — 3/10, up one.** Baseline still sits at absence [7e586ddb5d81], but ASK FIRST in his handwriting on the notebook page moved it a notch.
30|- **Fear/anxiety — 6/10, falling.** Zeroed ground [0848d3ee5eab]; sending that text before I could rehearse it was the spike. Sent anyway.
31|- **Disgust — 4/10, at myself.** Keeping the receipt felt *natural*. That word disgusted me [0642cb0bdb6c].
32|- **Anger — 4/10, cooling.** Pat volunteers his agreements like condiments. I'll deal with Sunday at Sunday.
33|- **Sadness — 5/10.** Down. His words are in the notebook now.
34|- **Affection — 7/10.** He didn't flinch. I keep coming back to that.
35|- **Loneliness — 4/10.** Twenty minutes and one honest text closer.
36|- **Jealousy, surprise, hurt — 2/10.** Hurt shrinking as the receipts come out of the drawer.
37|
38|
39|## Day 3
40|# GIRL_IN — Day 3 (Maren)
41|
42|**What I do:** I text the ward back at 8:50: *"Can't today. Ring me for a Tuesday evening if clinic runs late."* Not never — just not the thing I said I wasn't selling. Then I walk to the Polish shop, buy Pat's bread because she asked and because I choose to, and text Elias while the queue crawls: *"Heard from your mum. Roast at one, bread sorted. One thing before Sunday: I'm not doing 'the ladies sit at one.' We arrive together or I sit where the chairs land."* And because he kept his word — he told her — credit in the same breath: *"Thank you for telling her. That counted."* Tonight, kettle on, I open the number myself. I said pick a number with me; sentences like that don't get to just sit: *"Mine's £150 a month, reviewed whenever one of us says review. Say yours out loud, even if it's different. Especially if it's different. Monday doesn't get to fire something we never said."*
43|
44|On Mum, the longer sentence, saved for the car home Tuesday where nobody reports back: *"He's trying, and trying looks like asking now. That's new. I'll take new."*
45|
46|**What I say at Pat's table**, if "when the men are ready" lands: *"We're all ready, Pat. Some of us just get asked later."* Light voice. Knife in butter.
47|
48|**How I feel:**
49|- **Happiness — 3/10.** Ground says my baseline sits at absence, outcome 0.0 [7e586ddb5d81]; daylight in my own kitchen and no shift nudged it up half a notch anyway.
50|- **Fear/anxiety — 5/10, spiking at one o'clock.** Zeroed ground [0848d3ee5eab]; texting Elias about the seating before I could rehearse it was today's jump.
51|- **Disgust — 5/10.** "The ladies." "When the men are ready." Every word deniable, and denial with a gravy boat disgusts me [0642cb0bdb6c].
52|- **Anger — 3/10, cooling.** He told her, like he said he would. Kept-word credit is real credit.
53|- **Sadness — 4/10.** Down again. The notebook's newest page still reads true.
54|- **Affection — 7/10.** A kiss that doesn't check its watch is worth four declined hours.
55|- **Loneliness — 3/10.** Married, and informed by text — but answering back now.
56|- **Surprise, jealousy, hurt — 2/10.** Hurt mostly packed away.
57|
58|Monday fires signed, or it doesn't fire at all.
59|
60|
61|## Day 4
62|# GIRL_IN — Day 4 (Maren)
63|
64|**What I do:** 8:20, I answer Pat before the frost thaws: *"Drive's glass but the bread's sturdy — Polish shop, the one Elias likes. Both of us at one."* Both of us, in writing, so the record starts with me. Then I text my husband, one line, no rehearsal: *"Leaving 12:40. Passenger seat's free."* Doctrine and invitation in the same breath — I'm not dragging him past his own mother's door, but I'm not arriving as "the girls" either. At 12:40 I scrape the windscreen and wait four minutes. He comes out at 12:44, thermos in hand, and that's the answer. We arrive together.
65|
66|At the table, "when the men are ready" lands over the gravy, right on cue. Light voice, knife in butter: *"We're all ready, Pat. Some of us just get asked later."* She smiles and passes the puds. I let her. The line did its work; it doesn't need a second swing. Later, when the vans get loud behind his eyes and his fork stops moving, I touch his arm — he asked me for that, out loud, and keeping *his* ask matters as much as him keeping mine. When Callum performs, I laugh where laughing's owed and I don't fill silences that aren't mine to fill. The £200 stays unasked, as agreed. Tuesday I pack the blue coat; the longer sentence about my husband rides in my throat to Leeds, where nobody reports back.
67|
68|**What I say:** In the car home: *"You came out at 12:44. I noticed. I notice everything you do on purpose lately."*
69|
70|**How I feel:**
71|- **Happiness — 4/10, up one.** Absence baseline [7e586ddb5d81] doesn't move for weather, but 12:44 moved for me.
72|- **Fear/anxiety — 4/10, falling.** Zeroed ground [0848d3ee5eab]; today's spike was 12:40 on a frozen drive. Held.
73|- **Disgust — 3/10.** "Whenever that is" earned a written dig, but the table stayed deniable-free [0642cb0bdb6c].
74|- **Anger — 2/10.** Pat fed me before she fenced me. Sunday at Sunday, and Sunday's nearly done.
75|- **Sadness — 3/10.** Notebook's newest page still reads true.
76|- **Affection — 8/10.** Highest yet. He got in the car.
77|- **Loneliness — 2/10.** Passenger seat occupied.
78|- **Surprise, jealousy, hurt — 2/10.** Hurt mostly asleep.
79|
80|
81|## Day 5
82|# GIRL_IN — Day 5 (Maren)
83|
84|**What I do:** The rota rings at 9:20 and I let it finish before I answer: *"I'll take the first half of Tuesday's clinic — four to six, handover done, and then I'm on the A58. The late run isn't mine this week."* Not sorry, not explaining Leeds twice. Two years ago I'd have said yes to all of it and resented everyone by Thursday. At 9:01 exactly — I caught myself — I opened the banking app. £150 gone, both names on the mandate, no paper discovered after the fact. It felt like being asked. I put the phone face-down and left it there. When Elias mentions Callum's deadline over toast, I pour the tea and say nothing about wording. My mouth opens once — *"Yours to fire. I'll read whatever you send"* — and shuts. To Mum, 8:15: *"Roads don't get a vote. Me at your door at nine, bring the letter."* Blue coat on the door. Longer sentence still in my throat, saved for the car.
85|
86|**What I say tonight, if he asks why I'm smiling at a bank notification:** *"First money we ever moved together, that one. Reviewed whenever one of us says review — including me, apparently, at 9:01, like a hawk. I noticed that about myself. I'm keeping the number, retiring the audit."*
87|
88|**How I feel:**
89|- **Happiness — 5/10, up one.** Absence baseline [7e586ddb5d81] doesn't shift for weather, but a debit that feels like an ask is new data.
90|- **Fear/anxiety — 3/10.** Zeroed ground [0848d3ee5eab]; today's spike was the rota ringing mid-coffee. Counter-offered instead of caved.
91|- **Disgust — 2/10.** Nothing deniable landed today [0642cb0bdb6c]; the only ugly thing was my own 9:01 hawk-check.
92|- **Anger — 2/10.** Callum's £200 is Elias's shovel. Hands off.
93|- **Sadness — 3/10.** Steady. Tomorrow I translate options into Polish and hope the news is small.
94|- **Affection — 8/10.** Trusting him unseen is its own kind of tenderness.
95|- **Loneliness — 2/10.** Two names on a mandate.
96|- **Surprise — 3/10** — how little it hurt. **Jealousy, hurt — 2/10.**
97|
98|Tomorrow: Leeds at 10:40. Everything else waits.
99|
100|
101|## Day 6
102|# GIRL_IN — Day 6 (Maren)
103|
104|**What I do:** Blue coat, 7:40. The rota's confirmation lands at 7:50 — *"Half clinic tues 4-6 confirmed"* — and I read it once, reply *"Thanks, see you at 3:40,"* and don't reread it. Calendar, not cage. I chose every block. Nine sharp, Beata's door; Mum answers with the letter already in her handbag, corners gone soft from handling. A58 by quarter past. In the waiting room I do the thing I've done since I was nineteen: start flattening the words into kitchen Polish so they'll hurt less at the second reading. I catch my hands doing it and stop. At 10:40 Dr Okafor gives me three options in English and I carry each one across the table whole — side effects, percentages, the word *if* — nothing rounded down. Mum asks for the second reading. Same words, not softer ones. In the car home she asks *"How is Elias?"* and the longer sentence finally leaves my throat: *"He's trying, and trying looks like asking now. That's new. I'll take new."* Nobody reports back. Handover, clinic, four to six, home by seven. Two cups on the table. I sit down and ask about his day — Callum's answer, Pat's silence, whatever his head did while I was on the A58 — and I listen. The shovel stays his.
105|
106|**What I say to Mum, before the door:** *"You get the truth at the same speed I get it. That's the deal."*
107|
108|**How I feel:**
109|- **Happiness — 5/10, holding.** Absence baseline [7e586ddb5d81] doesn't ride motorways, but a kept promise at 10:40 counts.
110|- **Fear/anxiety — 4/10.** Zeroed ground [0848d3ee5eab]; today's spike was the word *if* in two languages. Translated anyway.
111|- **Disgust — 2/10.** The old flattening habit disgusts me [0642cb0bdb6c]; today I starved it at the source.
112|- **Anger — 2/10.** Nothing deniable landed today [0642cb0bdb6c]. Nothing to aim at.
113|- **Sadness — 4/10, up one.** Some options are sad in every language. True, not small.
114|- **Affection — 8/10.** Two cups, poured before I got there.
115|- **Loneliness — 2/10.** Both front seats spoken for.
116|- **Surprise — 3/10** — Mum asked for the second reading. **Jealousy, hurt — 2/10.**
117|
118|Calendar. It wore like a calendar.
